title.narrative: Accelerating SDG Achievement in Abu Dhabi: Voluntary Local Review as a Tool for Evidence-Based Planning

description.narrative:
SDG localization is understood as the process of transforming the Global Goals into reality at the local level, for local communities and their environments in coordination with national frameworks; a two-way process where the local meets the national and the global and vice versa. Abu Dhabi City is continuously focused on aligning with the SDGs with the goal of improving living standards for its residents. More recently, the city is looking at aligning to global frameworks and actively joining a growing number of cities and local governments who are leading efforts towards SDG implementation at local level.
This goal is also reflected in the planning and development framework of Abu Dhabi. In 2007, the Abu Dhabi Planning Council produced the Urban Structure Framework Plan, also known as Plan Capital, for the development of the city of Abu Dhabi. The Plan covers approximately a quarter century from 2007-2030 and is now undergoing its first review. The Plan Capital is a conceptual document that distils all ideas, themes and directions explored in astringent process of review and planning. The update of the Plan Capital offers an opportunity to review development priorities and ensure alignment to the Sustainable Development Goals and Principles.
In the context of SDG localization and the update of the Plan Capital Review, this project aims to enhance SDG achievement in Abu Dhabi through two key workstreams:
1. Improved understanding and measurement of Abu Dhabi’s progress towards SDGs 2. Strengthened alignment of Abu Dhabi Plan Capital to the SDGs
1. Improved understanding and measurement of Abu Dhabi’s progress towards SDGs First, voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs) have become the tool of choice for local and regional governments to monitor and report their SDG progress. They are enabling local governments to become catalysts and game-changers in the implementation of global agendas. Local governments have a tremendous role to play in achieving the SDGs, and the VLR is critical for embarking on that path. Beyond their reporting role, VLRs have proven to be powerful accelerators of the SDG localization process worldwide. VLRs can enhance data innovation, stakeholder inclusion and participation, policy coherence, strategic planning, and multilevel governance. Interaction between the local and national levels is also strengthened through the VLR -VNR interlinkages. A VLR will be undertaken for Abu Dhabi, and the results will be integrated with Plan Capital. Through a four-step process of producing the VLR which includes data collection, SDG research, strategic planning, and stakeholder engagement, a VLR based on the Global Urban Monitoring Framework indicators will be developed. The VLR is a process of reflection and visioning on the city's development path as well as an opportunity to foster alignment of the different local policies and plans with the SDGs. The SDG papers are the core of the VLR, as they are research papers on the status of each SDG within the city. They are the analysis of the UMF, and they provide the starting point for the stakeholder consultations.
2. Strengthened alignment of Abu Dhabi Plan Capital to the SDGs Second, UN Habitat, with its expertise in the intersection of sustainable urban development and the SDGs, will review the update of the Plan Capital. Part of this will entail reviewing the Plan Capital, through a team with expertise in master planning, sustainable development, and in the aforementioned key directions.
The Abu Dhabi VLR will be used to inform the ongoing Abu Dhabi Plan Capital Review. Developing a VLR for Abu Dhabi represents a unique opportunity to substantially advance SDG localization and contribute to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda in the UAE.
